Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). Visuals-only: gives the `ricochet` player weapon a distinct in-flight projectile look, per-shot VFX and fire/impact SFX through the shared bullet-shape seam.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the Ricochet's shots to render as a teardrop/streak pellet with a short trail, leaving a brief edge-flash on each bounce, so I can read at a glance which weapon I am holding and feel it when it fires and connects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Ricochet shot is a teardrop/streak pellet with a short trail, leaving a brief edge-flash on each bounce.
- **Per-weapon game feel.** Each weapon/attack child adds VFX **and** SFX for both fire and impact (muzzle flash / launch cue, trail where appropriate, impact flash + hit sound), consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic and the existing baked-cue audio pipeline (ToneForge `playCue`). The Ricochet's fire cue is newly baked ToneForge fire cue (currently missing from `playWeaponFireSound`) and its impact cue is newly baked ToneForge impact cue.
- Fire VFX (muzzle flash / launch cue) and any trail for `ricochet` are wired through the shared combat-core spawn path as cheap Graphics primitives in the `src/vfx/` style.
- A distinct impact flash + hit sound plays when a `ricochet` shot connects, routed through the shared impact path so game and gyms behave identically.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — per-shape rendering driven by the weapon definition
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `ricochet` visual metadata (shape/visual fields)
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — carry visual fields through level resolution unchanged
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — fire/impact cues
- `src/vfx/` — `ricochet` muzzle/trail/impact module(s)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — parity adoption

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Shared bullet-shape rendering seam (prerequisite child)

## Scope guard

Visuals/feel only. Any behaviour/balance change discovered while adding feel must be filed as a separate work item (`related-to:AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE`), not absorbed here.

# implement.py finish build step times out at 300 s (npm run build ~5 min due to audio render)

## Headline

The `implement.py finish` build gate aborts work items whose `npm run build`
exceeds the hard-coded 300 s timeout; on this repo the build takes ~5 min
because `build-audio` auto mode always re-renders all 65 baked WAVs. The fix:
make `build-audio` verify committed assets first and only re-render when the
audio inputs have actually changed, so the build is near-instant unless audio
sources moved.

## Problem

`run_build()` in `implement.py` executes `npm run build` with a fixed
`timeout=300`. On this repo `npm run build` runs `build-audio` (in default
`auto` mode), which **unconditionally re-renders every baked ToneForge
asset** whenever the ToneForge CLI is resolvable — measured 3.5–6 min for the
audio stage alone (machine-load dependent), plus `tsc --noEmit` (~7 s) and
vite build. `implement.py finish` therefore routinely aborts with
`Command '['npm', 'run', 'build']' timed out after 300 seconds` even though
the build itself is green, blocking finish for every work item that touches
the build.

The rendered output is **byte-deterministic**: re-rendering matches the
committed assets and checksums (a full build leaves no dirty tree). The only
defect is the wasted re-render and the wrapper timeout.

## Users

- **Implementing agent** running `implement.py finish <id>` — wants the
  automated build gate to pass when the build is genuinely green.
- **Producer/developer** working this repo — wants fast local builds and CI
  that does not re-render unchanged audio.
- **Repo maintainers of the audio pipeline** (future cue/recipe authors) —
  want a change to manifest/recipes/pin to still force a re-render.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py finish <id>` completes its build step without a spurious
  timeout on this repo (a ~5 min render no longer blocks finish).
- A fresh `npm run build` produces a **byte-identical artifact set**
  (committed WAVs + `checksums.json` unchanged) when no audio inputs changed.
- When any audio input (manifest, recipe, pin, seed block) changes,
  `build-audio` re-renders and the assets + checksums update deterministically.
- `--verify` still performs a strict checksum-only verification; explicit
  `--render` still forces a full re-render; auto mode's fast path is
  verifiable and documented.
- Existing audio pipeline tests pass; new tests cover the verify-first fast
  path (unchanged inputs → no render) and the changed-input re-render path.
- All related documentation updated (build-audio header comments, usage text,
  any docs referencing the auto-mode behaviour).
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must stay within the built-in determinism contract: assets are rendered
  twice and compared; re-render must produce identical checksums.
- `build-audio` fast path must fail closed on any checksum drift
  (verify mismatch must still abort the build, as today).
- The fix should be repo-local (in `scripts/build-audio.mjs`), not a change
  to the global `implement.py` skill, unless a complementary safety net is
  wanted later (operator chose the verify-first fast path over the
  configurable-timeout approach).
- Auto mode's current contract — render when ToneForge CLI is available,
  else verify — is superseded by verify-when-unchanged; keep `--render`
  (`npm run build-audio:render`) and `--verify`
  (`npm run build-audio:verify`) as explicit escape hatches.
- Respect the Gym↔game parity rule: audio behaviour is pipeline-level, so no
  gameplay divergence is introduced.

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `build` = `build-audio && tsc --noEmit && vite build && check-bundle`.
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (wrapper) → `scripts/build-audio.mjs`
  (deterministic WAV pipeline, AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD).
- `build-audio.mjs` modes: `auto` (render if ToneForge resolvable, else
  verify), `render`, `verify`. `verifyAssets()` already implements strict
  checksum verification against `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`
  (`assets`, `seedBlock`, `manifest`), including missing/unexpected/mismatch
  detection and stale-asset removal.
- 65 baked assets under `public/audio/sfx/`, `checksums.json` version 1.
- `implement.py` (global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`, git-tracked
  in the SorraAgents repo) `run_build()` uses `timeout=300`; test/push steps
  already resolve `timeoutPerCommand` from `.pi/test-config.json`
  (SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG).

## Desired change

Extend `build-audio.mjs` auto mode with a **verify-first fast path**:

1. Compute a deterministic fingerprint of the audio inputs — the manifest,
   recipe files, pin, and seed block (the inputs that fully determine
   rendered output).
2. Persist that fingerprint in `checksums.json` (e.g. an `inputs` or
   `fingerprint` field written during render).
3. In auto mode: if the committed `checksums.json` fingerprint matches the
   current on-disk inputs, run `verifyAssets()` only (fast, no render) and
   succeed; otherwise fall through to the existing full render (which
   updates assets + checksums, preserving determinism).
4. `--render` and `--verify` behave exactly as today; auto mode with no
   ToneForge CLI still degrades to verify as today.

This makes `npm run build` near-instant for unchanged audio, keeps drift
detection via `verifyAssets()`, and never approaches the 300 s wrapper
timeout in practice.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale/absent fingerprint (rollout risk, medium).** An existing
  `checksums.json` has no fingerprint field. Auto mode must treat a missing
  or unmatchable fingerprint as "inputs may have changed" and fall through
  to render (or explicit `--verify`), never fail the build on the fast path.
- **Fingerprint completeness (medium).** The fingerprint must cover *all*
  inputs that determine output (manifest, recipe files, pin, seed block); a
  missed input would let a change slip through without re-render. Mitigation:
  compute the fingerprint over the resolved input file set used by the
  renderer (same inputs `buildAssets()` reads), and keep the derivation
  unit-tested.
- **Verify-first must stay fail-closed.** Unchanged inputs → verify only;
  any checksum mismatch still aborts the build (existing `verifyAssets`
  behaviour, unchanged).
- **Assumption: audio sources are committed/git-tracked.** The fast path
  assumes the on-disk inputs reflect the working tree; a dirty recipe with
  an unchanged fingerprint is out of scope (declared, not silent).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Parallelising the render and the global
  `implement.py` timeout config are explicitly out of scope for this item;
  record as separate work items if desired (operator chose the fast path
  only).

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-audio.mjs` — auto-mode fast path + input fingerprint logic.
- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — hermetic tests for fast path,
  changed-input re-render, and preserved `--verify`/`--render` semantics.
- `scripts/build-audio.d.mts` — type declarations if new exports are added.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — gains the persisted input fingerprint.
- `package.json` — no script change expected (or document if `build-audio`
  default flag changes).

## Related work

- `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` — Implement build gate times out on the ~5-minute
  ToneForge audio render (open near-duplicate; closed as duplicate per
  operator decision — its "document the chosen mechanism" AC is folded into
  this item).
- `AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD` — Deterministic WAV build pipeline (builds the
  module being changed; completed).
- `AH-0MUZJDT88002L536` — Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve
  the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed; resolved ToneForge resolution in
  worktrees, context for auto-mode behaviour).
- `AH-0MUZ5HW310018DQR` — CI: Pages deploy npm ci fails under npm 10 due to
  file: ToneForge optional dependency (completed).
- `AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO` — Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene (completed;
  pin-check runs before auto mode).
- `SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG` — global implement.py per-repo timeout config
  precedent (referenced in code).
- `SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0` — Local skill extensions for global skills
  (the alternative repo-local extension mechanism; not needed for this
  fix since the change lives in the repo's own build scripts).

### Related work (automated report from /skill:find-related)

- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme
  and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed).
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** – GymDiver AC1 (diver x locked during dive) is
  wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load (completed; repository
  build/test-timing context).
- **AH-0MUTYV8RJ009MWKJ** – Audio playback contract tests (completed;
  audio output contract relevant to the baked-asset pipeline).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Two open work items describe the same 300 s build-gate timeout with
  overlapping ACs (`AH-0MV87694J009Z34V`, older/high priority/cross-referenced;
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E`, later/medium). How should they be consolidated?"
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A: Keep this item, close
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` as duplicate." Recommended option A matched.
- Q2: "Which fix approach? A) verify-only fast path in build-audio when
  committed assets match; B) configurable build timeout in implement.py;
  C) both; D) parallelise the render."
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A" — verify-only fast path in
  `build-audio`, repo-local, root-cause fix. Recommended option A matched.
  (Option B was noted as an acceptable future safety net, not taken now.)

# Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) provides the *evidence*
(batch reports with distribution statistics) but the *loop* around it is still
manual and error-prone. A designer who wants to tune a knob must, by hand:
(1) run a baseline batch, (2) edit a CSV, (3) re-run the identical command,
(4) diff the JSON/text reports and interpret per-metric deltas across a table
of distributions. Human error creeps in exactly where the tool exists to remove
it: forgetting to keep seeds identical, comparing reports from different batch
configs, or misreading which metrics actually moved. The acceptance-verification
run already had to do this diff by hand (see docs/BALANCING.md §Acceptance-verification run).

There is no automation that: records a baseline, applies a single proposed edit
(guided), re-runs against the *same* seeds/config, and produces a per-metric
before/after comparison with guidance on whether each delta looks like the
intended effect.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning becomes a fast, auditable loop instead of a manual chore.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, repeatable record of each tuning attempt (edit, config snapshot, before/after reports) so balance history can be reviewed and reverted.

## Expected behaviour

- A single entry point (e.g. an extension of `scripts/evaluate.mjs` or a peer `scripts/balance-tune.mjs`) that:
  1. Runs the baseline batch (identical seeds/config/policy) and captures the report.
  2. Optionally applies a single, guided edit to a balance CSV — either (a) a declarative edit supplied by the caller (e.g. `--set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6`) or (b) an interactive prompt; in all cases the tool can **restore** the original file on completion so the checkout stays clean.
  3. Re-runs the identical batch and emits a **before/after comparison** artifact (per-metric deltas: mean/median/stdDev per distribution, plus per-archetype kill and per-upgrade deltas) alongside both full reports.
  4. Prints a human-readable summary identifying the metrics that moved significantly and flags distribution-shape changes (e.g. stdDev growth = variance increase).
- No production runtime impact; all new logic stays in the dev/eval layer (`src/ai/eval/`, Node shell). Determinism guarantees are preserved byte-for-byte.

## Suggested approach

- Reuse the existing irreproducibility guard: the comparison must verify both batches used identical sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt) before reporting deltas — an empty diff check confirms no side effects.
- Pure diff/aggregation logic in the TS core (`src/ai/eval/`) with a thin shell wrapper; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (same constraint as the epic).
- Where CSV edit support lands, reuse the shared loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` via `hydrateBalanceConfig`) so the re-run reads the edited values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: One-command loop.** A documented command runs baseline, applies one guided CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep, and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report, and a versioned before/after comparison (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas, per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas).
- **AC2: Same-sweep guard.** The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs, and errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs (detects side effects).
- **AC3: Deterministic comparison.** Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; independently-derived (empty) deltas are zero.
- **AC4: Safe restore.** After the run the CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success **and** failure paths (or the user opted into keeping the edit), verified by test; the working tree is clean unless the user says otherwise.
- **AC5: Readable summary.** The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), with the same statistics echoed in the machine-readable artifact.
- **AC6: Tests.** Pure comparison/aggregation, the same-sweep guard, safe restore and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC7: Documentation.** `docs/BALANCING.md` gains a `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section with the worked example; README references it.
- **AC8: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

# Extend the headless arena to simulate the full shipped campaign (waves, levels, upgrades)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) reports full balance
statistics, but two fields in its versioned schema are never populated by a
real run because the headless arena does not model campaign progression or
upgrade selection:

1. **Limit #1 — wave/level progression is not simulated.** The arena models a
   *single fixed skirmish*: a seed-derived spawn reservoir of hostiles with no
   wave sequencer, no `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry
   events, and no level transitions. Consequently `waveReached` and
   `levelReached` are **always 0** in a batch report (observed on a live
   `--batch --games 10` run), so the campaign difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) cannot be tuned with this tool. Today the
   only influence the difficulty curve has is the number of hostile *reservoir*
   waves.
2. **Limit #2 — upgrade/power-up choice balance is not simulated.** The arena
   collects power-ups but never drives the upgrade-choice flow, so
   `choice_selected` events are absent and `upgradesSelected` is always
   `(none)` in the report. Per-upgrade balance therefore cannot be measured
   from bot runs.

The arena is intentionally a simplification (a "closed-loop headless arena,
not Phaser"), but the epic's own acceptance criteria claim the report captures
"wave/level reached" and "upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id)". They are
present in the schema but empty in practice. To balance **the full campaign
shipped in the game**, the harness must exercise the same wave/level sequencer
and upgrade-choice flow that the game does — through the shared core, not a
divergent copy.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want a bot batch to play the *same campaign the game ships* (all levels/waves, with upgrade choices), so I can tune per-wave difficulty targets and per-upgrade balance from evidence instead of intuition.
- **As the automated-balancing maintainer**, I want the arena to drive the shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system, so a change to those systems is measured by the batch.
- **As a producer**, I want the campaign-tuning evidence to come from the shipped campaign definition, so a report reflects what players experience.

## Scope

- Drive the **shared campaign/wave sequencer** (the system that consumes
  `difficulty-curves.csv` and the hand-authored `LEVELS`) inside the headless
  arena, emitting the real `wave_start` / `wave_cleared` / `level_cleared`
  telemetry the analyzer already understands, so `waveReached` and
  `levelReached` become meaningful distributions.
- Drive the **shared upgrade-choice flow** so the bot makes (or receives)
  upgrade selections and `choice_selected` events are emitted, populating
  `upgradesSelected` per choice id.
- Keep every piece of gameplay behaviour coming from the **shared core**
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, the upgrade-choice
  system) — no divergent copy. This is the gym↔game parity convention: an
  enabled behaviour must run the same code in a gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Document the fidelity boundary precisely: what is now modelled (campaign
  progression, upgrade choices) and what remains simplified (VFX, formations,
  rendering).

## Non-goals

- No production runtime changes.
- No rendering/Phaser dependency in the eval core (`src/ai/eval/` stays pure:
  no wall clock, no I/O).

## Suggested approach

- Prototype sequencer integration first (spike within the item): confirm the
  shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system can run headless under
  Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses.
- Emit the canonical telemetry records rather than inventing new event types so
  the existing metrics/balance-stats extraction picks them up unchanged.
- Extend the batch runner to optionally run a full campaign per seed (with a
  bounded tick budget), and report per-wave / per-level distributions.
- Reuse the existing determinism guarantees: same seed + config + policy ⇒
  byte-identical report, now covering the campaign path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: Campaign progression simulated.** A headless run plays through the shared wave/level sequencer using the shipped campaign definition (all levels and waves, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), emitting real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry. A batch report therefore shows non-zero, meaningful `waveReached` and `levelReached` distributions.
- **AC2: Upgrade choices simulated.** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3: Single source of truth.** The arena consumes the shared wave sequencer / upgrade-choice system directly (asserted by test and the existing duplicate-body/parity guards); no divergent copy of campaign, enemy, ship or upgrade stats exists in `src/ai/eval/`.
- **AC4: Determinism preserved.** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC5: Config sensitivity.** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.
- **AC6: Fidelity boundary documented.** `docs/BALANCING.md` (and/or `docs/EVALUATION.md`) states exactly what campaign behaviour is now modelled and what remains simplified, so consumers do not over-read the report.
- **AC7: Tests.** Campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC8: Bounded resources.** A full-campaign batch over ~100 games still completes in a practical time and bounded memory on a dev machine (incremental aggregation, per-run summaries only).
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** (code comments, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README).
- **AC10: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Fidelity risk:** running the real sequencer headless may pull in Phaser-coupled code. *Mitigation:* confirm the shared core's headless-safety during the spike; keep the pure eval layer free of rendering.
- **Scope-creep risk:** this item is about *simulating* the campaign, not retuning it. Actual tuning changes remain separate work items.
- **Parity risk:** a divergent arena copy would violate gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1). *Mitigation:* consume the shared core; rely on the existing equivalence guards.
- **Determinism risk:** campaign RNG (dynamic/curve generation) must derive from the run seed exactly as the game does. *Mitigation:* reuse `createSeededRng` and the game's seed derivation; test byte-identical replay.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — the framework this extends.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — the comparison loop that will consume these richer reports.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the schema; becomes directly comparable once campaign stats are populated.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on richer campaign evidence.
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

## Problem

Manual review of AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 (Bot steering model to consume live ShipConfig thruster values) reported: "When I click Watch Demo (or run a capture) the AI bot behaves totally differently to when I am watching it in the gym scene. The gym scene is correct."

- Both scenes build the brain via createCompetentBotBrain({ tunables: toCompetentOverrides(getCurrentBotTuningConfig().values) }) (PlayScene._applyBotTuning / GymBotTuning._applyTuning).

- The demo seam responds to a custom ShipConfig end-to-end (new tests in src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts).

The remaining 'totally different' behaviour is scenario-driven, not model-driven:
- The shipped demo (PlayScene) plays the live campaign: random offscreen asteroids (asteroidSpawnerEnabled=true), timed waves (getWaveState active → enemyWavePressurePort), lane traffic, harvesters, ghosts, boss encounters.
- The bot-tuning gym (GymBotTuning via generateRandomLevel) generates enemy-formation-only levels: the sequencer candidate pool filters out asteroid/harvester/grunt; there is no asteroid spawner, no timed waves and no boss.

## Goal

Make the bot-tuning gym exercise the same scenario pressures the shipped demo does — asteroids (with drift), timed waves, and optionally boss — so tuning in the gym transfers to the demo, and the demo does not behave 'totally differently' from the gym purely because of scenario content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. GymBotTuning (or the GymLevel base) can spawn drifting asteroids the same way PlayScene does (or reuse the shared spawn-planning helper), so the bot's hazard/asteroid responses are exercised.

# Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions

**Priority:** critical · **Issue type:** bug · **Stage:** intake

## Problem statement

Bot-tuning definitions live **only** in `window.localStorage` (key
`ai-hell-bot-tuning`, written by `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`), and the
shipped **Watch Demo** / attract mode (`PlayScene` demo mode) reads that store
when a demo starts. `localStorage` is per-browser, per-origin and per-machine —
it is not part of the repository or of a build. When the code is checked out on
another machine, or served from a distributed build (e.g. the GitHub Pages
alpha), a fresh browser has no saved state and every demo silently falls back
to the built-in `Default` config instead of the tuned Bot definitions the
developer has in their build environment. The enemy/ship/difficulty CSVs do
ship with the build (bundled via `?raw` in `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`); bot
tuning has no equivalent, which is why only bot behaviour is affected.

**Goal:** a Git-tracked bot-tuning configuration is bundled into every build as
the baseline, so distributed builds and fresh machines fly the correct Bot
definitions, while a local user's saved `localStorage` selection still wins
locally.

## Users

- **Developer / designer of the demo bot:** tunes named configurations in the
  Bot Tuning gym, and expects every build of the game — including one checked
  out or served on another machine — to fly those definitions rather than the
  generic factory defaults.
- **Producer / release reviewer:** runs demos and records gameplay video
  (`npm run capture`, `npm run record -- --bot`) from any checkout and expects
  the footage to show the tuned bot, not a default fallback.

Example user stories:

- *As a developer tuning the demo bot, I want the tuned configuration committed
  to the repo so that a fresh checkout, build and demo run plays my tuning
  without re-exporting anything.*
- *As a producer, I want the GitHub Pages alpha to show the correct bot
  behaviour so release footage and preview builds match the tuned design.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Bundled baseline ships and is used.** A Git-tracked bot-tuning
   configuration file (the exact exported store shape `{ version, current,
   configs }`) is committed and bundled into dev and production builds; in a
   browser with no (or corrupt/missing) `localStorage` state,
   `loadBotTuningState()` returns the bundled configuration set and the shipped
   demo (`PlayScene` demo mode) flies it.
2. **AC2 — Local overrides are preserved.** When `localStorage` holds a saved
   state, the currently-selected local configuration wins locally — precedence
   is `localStorage` → bundled baseline, mirroring the CSV config pattern; a
   fresh browser shows the bundled baseline, not factory defaults.
3. **AC3 — Corrupt-safe, unchanged fallback behaviour.** Missing/invalid
   `localStorage` (and an unreadable/invalid bundled file) never crashes or
   degrades demo behaviour; the store remains versioned and corrupt-safe.
4. **AC4 — Refresh workflow round-trips.** The bundled file is byte-equivalent
   to the Bot Tuning gym's **Export** output (via
   `serialiseBotTuningState()`), so *tune → Export → commit → build → fresh
   browser* reproduces the tuned demo; the workflow is documented.
5. **AC5 — Recording tools see the baseline.** `npm run capture` (demo path)
   and `npm run record -- --bot` launched without `--bot-config` in a fresh
   Chromium now record the bundled baseline (previously factory defaults);
   passing `--bot-config` still overrides for a specific clip.
6. **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit and integration tests cover the fallback
   and precedence; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass; the gym↔game
   duplicate-body parity guard stays green.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`,
   `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12).
8. **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No changes to bot *decision* code — only which tunables construct the
  brain/governor (consistent with AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL non-goals).
- The store's persistence model stays `localStorage`; the bundled file is a
  baseline fallback, not a new write path.
- The shipped file must be **Git-tracked** (never git-ignored).
- Normal (human) Play Game sessions stay untouched — the bot seam remains
  inert outside demo mode.
- No schema/version bump is expected (`BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` shape is
  reused).

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `createDefaultState()` seeds only the built-in
  `Default` config; `parseState()` already validates the exact exported
  `{ version, current, configs }` shape and is corruption-safe, so a bundled
  JSON blob can reuse it.
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — the established bundling point for Git-tracked
  design data (`?raw` CSV imports consumed by production/static builds).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — demo mode already calls
  `getCurrentBotTuningConfig()` on start and rebuilds the brain/governor
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL); no change needed there.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/record-session.mjs` — launch a
  fresh Chromium; inject `--bot-config` only when the flag is passed.
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (§ Bot-tuning configuration),
  `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (§12).

## Desired change

1. **Add the shipped baseline.** Commit a new `src/data/bot-tuning.json` holding
   the exported store state (produced via the gym's **Export** button /
   `serialiseBotTuningState()` from the developer's build environment) and
   export it from `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` (JSON import or a `?raw` parse,
   matching how the CSVs bundle).
2. **Make it the fallback.** In `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`,
   `createDefaultState()` / `parseState()` no longer default to the lone
   factory `Default` when storage is empty; instead the bundled file is parsed
   through the existing `parseState()` validation (which already falls back
   safely on malformed input) so a fresh browser seeds the bundled
   configurations — keeping a `Default`-named entry that carries the shipped
   values so the gym selector and config-name reporting are unchanged.
   Precedence stays `localStorage` → bundled baseline.
3. **Docs.** Document the baseline, the precedence rule, and the refresh
   workflow (tune → Export → overwrite `src/data/bot-tuning.json` → commit).
4. **Tests.** Add store tests (no storage / corrupt storage / invalid bundled
   file → bundled baseline; saved storage wins), a demo-mode test asserting the
   demo flies the bundled baseline in a fresh profile, and keep capture-script
   tests green.

## Key Files

- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — **new**, Git-tracked baseline (exported store
  shape).
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — export the bundled bot-tuning baseline.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — seed from the bundled baseline when storage is
  empty/invalid.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.test.ts` — new baseline/precedence cases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / demo-mode integration test — verify the fresh
  profile demo flies the bundled baseline.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — unchanged code; verify fresh-browser capture
  uses the baseline (test/doc only).
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`,
  `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`.

## Related work

- `Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL)` —
  completed; introduced the localStorage store read by demo mode and the
  `--bot-config` flow. This bug is the distribution gap that feature left open.
- `Gym scene for AI bot tuning (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0)` — completed; the tuning
  gym + store.
- `Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L)` /
  `Create a CSV file to maintain enemy configurations (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)` —
  completed; the CSV bundling pattern this fix mirrors.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "the correct Bot definitions" are the Bot Tuning gym's named
  configurations (confirmed with the operator).
- **Assumption:** the shipped baseline should apply identically in dev and
  production/distributed builds, with local `localStorage` overriding locally
  (confirmed with the operator).
- **Risk — stale baseline:** the committed file can drift from current tuning.
  *Mitigation:* document the refresh workflow; keep the file as the single
  source of the shipped baseline (like the CSVs).
- **Risk — surprising local overrides:** a user who previously saved the old
  `Default` values in `localStorage` keeps them locally. *Mitigation:* expected
  and consistent with the CSV/localStorage precedence; documented.
- **Scope creep — automatic sync** of local gym edits back to the repo (a
  dev-mode write path analogous to the CSV plugin) is **out of scope** here and
  should be recorded as a separate work item if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What are the 'Bot definitions' that should travel?" — Answer (producer,
  interactive): "A — the Bot Tuning gym's named configurations
  (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`) that Watch Demo / attract mode flies."
  Source: interactive reply. Research: `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` is the only
  persistence; demo mode in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_applyBotTuning`)
  reads it; CSVs ship via `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`.
- Q: "How should the tuned bot definition reach a distributed build?" —
  Answer (producer, interactive): "A — commit a Git-tracked bot-tuning config
  file, bundled into the build like the CSVs (baseline), with localStorage
  still able to override locally." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "On a fresh machine/browser, which should win?" — Answer (producer,
  interactive): "A — the shipped baseline config is the effective default; a
  user's local localStorage selection overrides it locally (mirrors the CSV
  pattern)." Source: interactive reply.
